subject: Meeks et al. (2000)
object: Meeks et al. (2000) performed a genome scan in 5 Arabic families with primary ciliary dyskinesia. Using GENEHUNTER, they obtained a maximal multipoint lod score (HLOD) of 4.4 on chromosome 19q13.3-qter at alpha (proportion of linked families) = 0.7. Recombinations at D19S572 and D19S218 defined a 15-cM critical region.

subject: Meeks et al. (2000)
object: Meeks et al. (2000) stated that their data gave significant evidence for a PCD locus on chromosome 19q and confirmed locus heterogeneity. The estimated proportion of linked families was 0.7.

subject: Meeks et al. (2000)
object: Meeks et al. (2000) described primary ciliary dyskinesia as an autosomal recessive condition with chronic sinusitis, bronchiectasis, and subfertility. They reported that situs inversus occurs in 50% of cases (Kartagener syndrome) and that the estimated incidence is 1 in 20,000 live births. They stated that the condition is caused by defective ciliary function with ultrastructural abnormalities, including absent dynein arms, absent radial spokes, and disturbed ciliary orientation.

subject: Mitchison et al. (2012)
object: Mitchison et al. (2012) noted that DNAAF3 (previously C19orf51) on chromosome 19q13 lies within the CILD2 locus mapped in consanguineous Arabic-origin PCD families with immotile cilia and absent outer dynein arms; affected individuals in 2 of the 3 originally linked families showed large regions of marker homozygosity across the DNAAF3 locus.

subject: Mitchison et al. (2012)
object: Mitchison et al. (2012) studied 10 patients from 3 consanguineous families (2 Arabic-origin families and a UK-Pakistani first-cousin family) with PCD due to DNAAF3 mutations, presenting with neonatal respiratory distress, recurrent cough and wheezing, nasal discharge, chest infections, sinusitis, otitis media, nasal polyps and bronchiectasis. Four of the 10 had situs inversus. Electron microscopy showed reduced or absent inner and outer dynein arms, and nasal cilia were immotile in all affected individuals; the authors noted the disorder was associated with male infertility.

subject: Mitchison et al. (2012)
object: In affected members of consanguineous Arabic-origin family UCL89 with CILD2, Mitchison et al. (2012) identified a homozygous c.323T>C transition in exon 3 of DNAAF3, resulting in a leu108-to-pro (L108P) substitution at a highly conserved residue. The variant was absent from 148 population-matched Arabic control chromosomes and from dbSNP, 1000 Genomes and NHLBI-ESP, was predicted probably damaging, and segregated with recessive inheritance (parents and unaffected sibs heterozygous).

subject: Mitchison et al. (2012)
object: In affected members of Arabic-origin family UCL66/67 with CILD2, Mitchison et al. (2012) identified a homozygous c.406C>T transition in exon 4 of DNAAF3, resulting in an arg136-to-ter (R136X) nonsense substitution. The variant was absent from 148 Arabic control chromosomes and from dbSNP, 1000 Genomes and NHLBI-ESP, and unaffected parents and sibs were heterozygous.

subject: Mitchison et al. (2012)
object: Among 112 additional PCD families screened, Mitchison et al. (2012) found that affected members of a first-cousin UK-Pakistani family (UCL71) showing linkage to the chromosome 19 locus carried a homozygous 1-bp insertion in exon 6 of DNAAF3 (c.762_763insT), predicted to cause a frameshift and premature termination (p.Val255CysfsX12). The variant was absent from 172 UK-Pakistani control chromosomes and segregated with the disorder.

subject: Mitchison et al. (2012)
object: Mitchison et al. (2012) found a homozygous c.973G>A (p.Ala325Thr) variant in DNAAF3 in a Belgian PCD patient, but considered it likely a Caucasian polymorphism because it was found on 1 of 192 Caucasian control chromosomes, was predicted benign, and affected a nonconserved residue.

subject: Mitchison et al. (2012)
object: Mitchison et al. (2012) found by immunofluorescence that outer dynein arm components DNAH5, DNAH9 and DNAI2 and the inner dynein arm light chain DNALI1 were absent from respiratory cilia of patients with DNAAF3 mutations, with residual DNAH5 and DNALI1 in the apical cytoplasm in some patients, suggesting that DNAAF3 is required for cytoplasmic preassembly of outer and inner dynein arms along the entire axoneme.

subject: Mitchison et al. (2012)
object: Mitchison et al. (2012) found that the Chlamydomonas pf22 mutant, carrying a nonsense mutation (p.Trp79X) in the DNAAF3 ortholog, had paralyzed half-length flagella lacking outer dynein arms and inner dynein arms b and c; PF22 was exclusively cytoplasmic. In pf22 cytoplasm, IC2 was hyperabundant and heavy chain-intermediate chain complexes formed abnormally, suggesting PF22 acts at a later step of dynein preassembly than PF13 and ODA7.

subject: Mitchison et al. (2012)
object: Mitchison et al. (2012) found that morpholino knockdown of dnaaf3 in zebrafish caused immotile olfactory placode cilia with reduced or missing dynein arms, body axis curvature, hydrocephalus, pronephric cysts, otolith defects, and left-right patterning defects, with about half of dnaaf3MOex8 embryos showing reversed or absent heart looping.
